import numpy as np

# Get poses and extents of both cubes
red_pos, _, red_extent = get_object_pose("red cube", return_bbox_extent=True)
green_pos, _, green_extent = get_object_pose("green cube", return_bbox_extent=True)

# Sample a grasp pose for the red cube and grasp it with an approach from above
grasp_pos, grasp_quat = sample_grasp_pose("red cube")
open_gripper()
goto_pose(grasp_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.10)
close_gripper()

# Lift the red cube straight up to clear the scene
lift_pos = grasp_pos.copy()
lift_pos[2] += 0.15
goto_pose(lift_pos, grasp_quat)

# Compute placement: gripper offset relative to red cube center is (grasp_pos - red_pos).
# Target red cube center is on top of the green cube: green top + half red height.
grasp_offset = grasp_pos - red_pos
target_red_center = green_pos.copy()
target_red_center[2] = green_pos[2] + green_extent[2] / 2.0 + red_extent[2] / 2.0
place_pos = target_red_center + grasp_offset

# Move above the green cube, then descend gently to the exact placement height
goto_pose(place_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.10)

# Release the cube only once it is resting on the green cube
open_gripper()

# Retreat upward
retreat_pos = place_pos.copy()
retreat_pos[2] += 0.10
goto_pose(retreat_pos, grasp_quat)

content.text:
You are controlling a Franka Emika robot with API described below.
Goal: Gently place the red cube on top of the green cube and then open the gripper. Nothing should be dropped from a height.
Use the extent of the cubes to calculate the exact height for placement.
You may write python code comments for reasoning but ONLY write the executable Python code and do not write it in code fences.
The functions (APIs) below are already imported to the environment. If you want to use numpy, scipy, torch, etc. you need to import them explicitly.

APIs:

get_object_pose(object_name: str, return_bbox_extent: bool = False) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray | None]
  Doc:
    Get the pose of an object in the environment from a natural language description.
    The quaternion from get_object_pose may be unreliable, so disregard it and use the grasp pose quaternion OR (0, 0, 1, 0) wxyz as the gripper down orientation if using this for placement position.
    
    Args:
        object_name: The name of the object to get the pose of.
    
    Returns:
        position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
        quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.
        bbox_extent: (3,) object extent in meters of x, y, z axes respectively in the world frame (full side length, not half-length extent). If return_bbox_extent is False, returns None.

sample_grasp_pose(object_name: str) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray]
  Doc:
    Sample a grasp pose for an object in the environment from a natural language description.
    Do use the grasp sample quaternion from sample_grasp_pose.
    
    Args:
        object_name: The name of the object to sample a grasp pose for.
    
    Returns:
        position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
        quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.

goto_pose(position: numpy.ndarray, quaternion_wxyz: numpy.ndarray, z_approach: float = 0.0) -> None
  Doc:
    Go to pose using Inverse Kinematics.
    There is no need to call a second goto_pose with the same position and quaternion_wxyz after calling it with z_approach.
    Args:
        position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
        quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.
        z_approach: (float) Z-axis distance offset for goto_pose insertion approach motion. Will first arrive at position + z_approach meters in Z-axis before moving to the requested pose. Useful for more precise grasp approaches. Default is 0.0.
    Returns:
        None

open_gripper() -> None
  Doc:
    Open gripper fully.
    
    Args:
        None

close_gripper() -> None
  Doc:
    Close gripper fully.
    
    Args:
        None

import numpy as np

# Verify the final state without moving the robot: check that the red cube rests on top of the green cube.
red_pos, _, red_extent = get_object_pose("red cube", return_bbox_extent=True)
green_pos, _, green_extent = get_object_pose("green cube", return_bbox_extent=True)

expected_red_z = green_pos[2] + green_extent[2] / 2.0 + red_extent[2] / 2.0
xy_offset = np.linalg.norm(red_pos[:2] - green_pos[:2])
z_error = red_pos[2] - expected_red_z

print("red cube position:", red_pos, "extent:", red_extent)
print("green cube position:", green_pos, "extent:", green_extent)
print("xy offset between cube centers (m):", xy_offset)
print("red cube z error vs expected stacked height (m):", z_error)
print("stacked:", xy_offset < 0.02 and abs(z_error) < 0.01)

import numpy as np

# Previous attempt left the red cube on the table ~7 cm from the green cube, so the grasp/placement failed.
# Retry: re-grasp the red cube, carry it above the green cube, descend to the exact stacked height, release.
red_pos, _, red_extent = get_object_pose("red cube", return_bbox_extent=True)
green_pos, _, green_extent = get_object_pose("green cube", return_bbox_extent=True)

grasp_pos, grasp_quat = sample_grasp_pose("red cube")
open_gripper()
goto_pose(grasp_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.10)
close_gripper()

# Lift straight up
lift_pos = grasp_pos.copy()
lift_pos[2] += 0.15
goto_pose(lift_pos, grasp_quat)

# Gripper-to-cube-center offset (keep full offset so the cube center lands on the green cube center)
grasp_offset = grasp_pos - red_pos

# Target red cube center: directly above green cube, resting on its top face
target_red_center = green_pos.copy()
target_red_center[2] = green_pos[2] + green_extent[2] / 2.0 + red_extent[2] / 2.0
place_pos = target_red_center + grasp_offset

# Move above the green cube, then descend to the placement height before releasing
goto_pose(place_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.10)
open_gripper()

# Retreat upward
retreat_pos = place_pos.copy()
retreat_pos[2] += 0.10
goto_pose(retreat_pos, grasp_quat)

# Verify
red_pos2, _, red_extent2 = get_object_pose("red cube", return_bbox_extent=True)
green_pos2, _, green_extent2 = get_object_pose("green cube", return_bbox_extent=True)
expected_red_z = green_pos2[2] + green_extent2[2] / 2.0 + red_extent2[2] / 2.0
xy_offset = np.linalg.norm(red_pos2[:2] - green_pos2[:2])
z_error = red_pos2[2] - expected_red_z
print("grasp_pos:", grasp_pos, "red_pos at grasp:", red_pos, "offset:", grasp_offset)
print("red cube position:", red_pos2, "green cube position:", green_pos2)
print("xy offset (m):", xy_offset, "z error (m):", z_error)
print("stacked:", xy_offset < 0.02 and abs(z_error) < 0.01)
